stops.note: to rebuild, to renew, from re- (again) and staurare (to erect, related to stare)
carried into French for restoring strength, especially through food
stops.meaning: to restore strength, especially through food

stops.note: a restorative food or broth, later a place serving such food, present participle of restaurer
adopted directly for an establishment where meals are served
stops.meaning: an establishment where meals are served to customers

current_meaning: a business establishment where meals are prepared and served to paying customers
